# osm-navit

**Navit's binary maps, converted from your OpenStreetMap regions, and its configuration**

- **Version recorded:** station
- **Categories:** `navigation-maps`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.navit-project.org/>
- **Needs first:** `osm-regions`, `navit`

## What it does

Converts each region `osm-regions` downloaded into Navit's own binary map format with `maptool`, one `.bin` per region under /usr/local/share/hammunition/data/osm-navit/, and writes the Navit configuration the `navit-offline` launcher opens there too: Debian's /etc/navit/navit.xml with speech set to espeak-ng and these maps added.

## Why you would want it

Navit cannot read OpenStreetMap's `.osm.pbf` files directly, so without this step the downloaded regions are no use to it. Doing it here means the conversion is recorded like any other install, repeated only when a region's data changed, and undone by `hammunition uninstall`, instead of being a hand-run command whose output nobody tracks.

## Before it will work

`osm-regions` with at least one region set in station config, and `navit` for `maptool`; both install first. With no regions set this unit is deferred by name along with `osm-regions`, and Navit still installs.

## How it installs

- converted from osm-regions by navit-maptool (ODbL-1.0, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright)

## Known problems

How long a conversion takes and how large the converted map is have not yet been measured on hardware; a large state may take a long time and needs free disk space beyond the download. Whether Navit routes across two separately converted regions has not yet been measured either. A region removed from station config has its converted map removed on the next install. The converted maps carry the same Open Database License obligations as the data they came from.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- Follows osm-regions: a region whose downloaded file changed is converted again on the next install, and one that did not is skipped.

## Where to get help with the software itself

The Navit wiki (https://wiki.navit-project.org/), which documents maptool, and the project's GitHub issues (https://github.com/navit-gps/navit/issues).
